gloss: shrine building; main hall of a Shinto shrine

definitions.gloss: shrine building; main hall of a Shinto shrine
definitions.explanation: The main building or buildings of a Shinto shrine where the deity is enshrined. Can refer to the main hall specifically or to the shrine buildings collectively.

examples.japanese: {社殿|しゃでん}に{参拝|さんぱい}する。
examples.english: To worship at the shrine building.

examples.japanese: {朱塗|しゅぬ}りの{社殿|しゃでん}が{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: The vermilion-painted shrine building is beautiful.

examples.japanese: {火災|かさい}で{焼失|しょうしつ}した{社殿|しゃでん}が、{数年|すうねん}かけて{再建|さいけん}された。
examples.english: The shrine building that was destroyed by fire was rebuilt over several years.

notes:
A compound of {社|しゃ} (shrine) and {殿|でん} (hall, palace). Refers specifically to Shinto shrine architecture, not Buddhist temples.

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
Shinto shrine buildings typically include the {本殿|ほんでん} (main hall housing the deity), {拝殿|はいでん} (worship hall where visitors pray), and various auxiliary structures. {社殿|しゃでん} can refer to any of these or to the complex as a whole. Traditional shrine architecture features distinctive elements like {千木|ちぎ} (forked finials) and {鰹木|かつおぎ} (log-shaped ridge ornaments).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {社殿|しゃでん}を{建|た}てる — to build a shrine hall
- {社殿|しゃでん}を{再建|さいけん}する — to rebuild a shrine hall
- {社殿|しゃでん}の{造営|ぞうえい} — construction of a shrine building
- {朱塗|しゅぬ}りの{社殿|しゃでん} — vermilion-painted shrine building

RELATED TERMS:
- {本殿|ほんでん} — main hall of a shrine; where the deity resides
- {拝殿|はいでん} — worship hall; where visitors pray
- {仏殿|ぶつでん} — Buddhist temple hall; the Buddhist equivalent
